content: It includes studies, guidelines, and reports related to mental health, disaster response, humanitarian aid, and healthcare ethics. 1. A study published in the Journal of Affective Disorders in April 2014 examined the prevalence of stress disorders and depressive symptoms among adult survivors of the Haiti earthquake, 30 months after the disaster. 2. Phillips SJ and Knebel A edited a comprehensive guide titled Mass Medical Care with Scarce Resources: A Community Planning Guide, published by the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality in 2007 under contract No. 290-04-0010. 3. The Institute of Medicine (IOM) released a framework in 2012 titled Crisis Standards of Care: A Systems Framework for Catastrophic Disaster Response, which provides guidance for healthcare systems during large-scale emergencies. 4. MacNeil A and colleagues conducted a study on the clinical features and mortality rates associated with Bundibugyo Ebola virus infection in Uganda, published in Emerging Infectious Diseases in December 2010. 5. The New England Journal of Medicine published a study in November 2014 on the clinical outcomes of Ebola patients in Sierra Leone, conducted by the KGH Lassa Fever Program, the Viral Hemorrhagic Fever Consortium, and the WHO Clinical Response Team. 6. Dallatomasina S and colleagues analyzed the epidemiology, clinical features, and outcomes of the Ebola outbreak in rural West Africa, with findings published in Tropical Medicine & International Health in April 2015. 7. Mollica RF and collaborators discussed the mental health challenges in complex emergencies in a December 2004 article in The Lancet, emphasizing the psychological impact of disasters and conflicts. 8. Angeletti C and colleagues explored the prevalence of pain among earthquake survivors in a study published in Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation, and Emergency Medicine in June 2012. 9. Downar J and Secareccia D highlighted the importance of palliative care during pandemics in a February 2010 article in Journal of Pain and Symptom Management, emphasizing that all patients must receive care. 10. Roy N and colleagues conducted a follow-up study on the surgical and psychosocial outcomes of rural victims of the 2001 earthquake, published in Injury in August 2005. 11. Rieder H and Elbert T examined the relationship between organized violence, family violence, and mental health in a community-based survey in Rwanda, published in European Journal of Psychotraumatology in November 2013. 12. Wu Z and colleagues investigated the psychological consequences and risk factors among adult survivors of the 2008 Wenchuan earthquake, with findings published in BMC Psychiatry in April 2014. 13. Kristensen P and colleagues reviewed the mental health effects of bereavement following sudden and violent losses, published in Psychiatry in Spring 2012. 14. Li J and colleagues studied the prevalence and risk factors of complicated grief among Sichuan earthquake survivors, with results published in Journal of Affective Disorders in April 2015. 15. Caffo E and Belaise C explored the psychological impact of traumatic injuries on children and adolescents in a July 2003 article in Child and Adolescent Psychiatric Clinics of North America. 16. Catani C and colleagues examined the effects of extreme stress on children’s mental health in Sri Lanka, focusing on family violence, war, and natural disasters, published in BMC Psychiatry in May 2008. 17. West TE and von Saint André-von Arnim A provided an overview of the clinical presentation and management of severe Ebola virus disease in a November 2014 article in Annals of the American Thoracic Society. 18. Teodorescu DS and colleagues conducted a cross-sectional study on chronic pain among multi-traumatized refugees resettled in Norway, published in BMC Psychology in March 2015. 19. The World Health Organization (WHO) published guidelines in 2013 for managing conditions specifically related to stress, emphasizing the importance of mental health interventions. 20. The WHO Model List of Essential Medicines (19th edition) outlines the medications necessary for addressing global health needs, with the document accessed in March 2018. 21. Dowell D and colleagues published the CDC Guideline for Prescribing Opioids for Chronic Pain in the United States in 2016, featured in JAMA. 22. Joranson D and colleagues developed guidelines to ensure patient access to controlled medicines while maintaining safe management practices, with the document accessed in March 2018. 23. The WHO, in collaboration with the War Trauma Foundation and World Vision International, released a guide on psychological first aid for field workers in 2011. 24. Atif N and colleagues conducted a qualitative study on the barriers and facilitators to delivering maternal mental health care through peer volunteers in Pakistan, published in International Journal of Mental Health Systems in March 2016. 25. Belkin GS and colleagues proposed the 5x5 implementation model for scaling up community mental health care in low-income regions, published in Psychiatric Services in 2011. 26. Patel V and colleagues discussed the integration of mental health services into primary healthcare platforms as a grand challenge in global health, published in PLOS Medicine in 2013. 27. Weobong B and colleagues evaluated the cost-effectiveness and sustained impact of the Healthy Activity Programme, a brief psychological treatment for depression delivered by lay counselors, published in PLOS Medicine. 28. Jones L explored grief and loss in societies affected by conflict and disaster in a chapter from the book edited by David Southall, published by Radcliffe Publishing in 2015. 29. Hudson P and colleagues developed guidelines for providing psychosocial and bereavement support to family caregivers of palliative care patients, published in Journal of Palliative Medicine in 2012. 30. Horwitz AV distinguished between distress and disorder as psychological outcomes of stressful social arrangements in a July 2007 article in Health (London). 31. Jones L and colleagues reviewed the prevalence of severe mental disorders in complex emergencies, published in The Lancet in August 2009. 32. Ezard N conducted a literature review on substance use among populations displaced by conflict, published in Disasters in July 2012. 33. Rose SC and colleagues evaluated the effectiveness of psychological debriefing for preventing post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in a Cochrane Database Systematic Review. 34. The United Nations General Assembly adopted Resolution 46/182 to strengthen the coordination of humanitarian emergency assistance. 35. The Sphere Project developed a training package to improve humanitarian response, with materials accessed in March 2018. 36. The United Nations published the International Drug Control Conventions in 2013, outlining global policies on controlled substances. 37. Berterame S and colleagues conducted a global study on the use of and barriers to accessing opioid analgesics, published in The Lancet in 2016. 38. The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs released the UNDAC Field Handbook in 2013 to guide disaster assessment and coordination. 39. The WHO published a framework for strengthening health systems to improve health outcomes, emphasizing the importance of universal access to healthcare. 40. Asgary R and Lawrence K conducted a qualitative study on the experiences and perspectives of medical humanitarians, published in BMJ Open in 2014. 41. Cardozo BL and Salama P discussed the mental health challenges faced by humanitarian aid workers in complex emergencies in a chapter from a book published by Baywood Publishing in 2002. 42. Blanchtière P explored the resilience of humanitarian workers in a report accessed in February 2018. 43. Haik J and colleagues studied the prevalence of burnout and compassion fatigue among Israeli burn clinicians, published in Neuropsychiatric Disease and Treatment in 2017. 44. Ehrenreich JH discussed the role of humanitarian aid organizations in managing stress among aid workers in a chapter from the Handbook of International Disaster Psychology. 45. Young PD and Rushton CH analyzed the concept of moral resilience in a September-October 2017 article in Nursing Outlook. 46. Salama P provided practical suggestions for maintaining the psychological health of relief workers in a report accessed in April 2018. 47. Jackson D and colleagues reviewed personal resilience as a strategy for thriving in the face of workplace adversity, published in Journal of Advanced Nursing in October 2007. 48. The WHO released an information sheet on mental health in the workplace, emphasizing the importance of supportive environments for employees. 49. Hunt MR and colleagues examined the experiences of healthcare professionals with ethics training in international aid work, published in Public Health Ethics in 2012. 50. Elsharkawi H and colleagues described a Red Cross/Red Crescent field training model for preparing humanitarian workers for disaster response. 51. The WHO published guidance for managing ethical issues in infectious disease outbreaks in 2016. 52. The WHO released a report on ethics in epidemics, emergencies, and disasters, focusing on research, surveillance, and patient care. 53. Etienne M and colleagues reflected on healthcare ethics following the Haitian earthquake, published in American Journal of Disaster Medicine in 2010. 54. The Australian Red Cross emphasized the importance of localizing the research process in a report accessed in February 2018. 55. The WHO published a guide for planning and implementing palliative care services, aimed at program managers. 56. The Declaration of Helsinki outlines ethical principles for medical research involving human subjects, emphasizing the importance of informed consent and patient welfare. 57. The WHO and other organizations have established ethical principles for healthcare during armed conflicts and emergencies, ensuring the protection of human rights. 58. The United Nations recognizes health as a fundamental human right, emphasizing the importance of access to medical, psychological, and related knowledge for all individuals.
